about: The painted court cards and jokers of Kit.card (cards/*.webp). scripts/cards/gen.py makes a picture from these: the style (jstyle for the joker), the suit palette, the card brief and the tail; the black-and-white joker (JKB) is an edit of the color joker (JK) with bw. "used" is the exact prompt of the picture now in the game.
style: A court card figure for a luxury deck of playing cards, painted by a master illustrator in fine gouache and oil: confident visible brushwork, rich but controlled colour, real light falling from the upper left, solid modelled form, a face painted with character like a portrait by Holbein or Clouet. The costume is the traditional dress of the English playing-card court: Tudor brocade robes with bold bands of colour and pattern, ermine trim, a jewelled collar, a crown or cap of gold. Portrait picture. The figure is seen from the hips up and fills the width: the top of the headgear sits a little below the top edge, the shoulders reach close to the left and right edges, the head is in the upper middle, and everything that matters (the headgear, the face, both hands and the thing held) lies in the upper two thirds of the picture; the lower third is only the robe. Background: a plain warm ivory ground, lightly brushed, with no scenery, no room and no sky. Painted, not vector, not cartoon, not anime, not digital airbrush, not glossy, no plastic skin, no soft glow.
jstyle: A court jester for the Joker of a luxury deck of playing cards, painted by a master illustrator in fine gouache and oil: confident visible brushwork, rich but controlled colour, real light falling from the upper left, solid modelled form, a face painted with character like a portrait by Holbein or Clouet, in the Tudor period. Background: a plain warm ivory ground, lightly brushed, with no scenery, no room and no sky. Painted, not vector, not cartoon, not anime, not digital airbrush, not glossy, no plastic skin, no soft glow.

tail: Correct anatomy: two arms, two hands with five fingers each, the hands in natural proportion to the head; any sword, axe, sceptre or staff is held by its grip in a closed hand, in a way a person could really hold it, and it is one straight, solid object. No text, no letters, no numbers, no suit symbols, no card border, no frame, no corner ornaments.

KH.brief: The King of Hearts, the 'suicide king' of the standard deck: a broad-faced king of about sixty with long wavy white hair and a white beard on his chin and jaw only: his upper lip is bare and shaved clean, with no moustache at all (the King of Hearts is the one king without a moustache). He faces the viewer. His right hand is raised beside his head holding the hilt of a sword, and the long straight blade passes diagonally behind his head so its tip seems to vanish behind the back of his skull, exactly as on the traditional card, with no wound and no blood. His left hand rests at his chest. A tall gold crown with crosses and fleurs.

JK.brief: The Joker: a court jester of about thirty-five, a wiry man with a sharp, clever, amused face, a long nose and laughing eyes, standing and facing the viewer, seen from his cap down to his knees. He wears a fool's cap with exactly three floppy points (one falling to the left, one rising in the middle and curling over, one falling to the right) and a small gold bell at the tip of each of the three points, a pointed ruff, and particoloured motley: one side crimson red and one side black, with gold diamonds. He holds a marotte (a short stick topped with a small carved jester's head) upright in front of his chest in his right hand, close to his body, and his left hand rests on his hip with the elbow tucked in. The figure is slim and upright: the whole figure, the marotte and both elbows included, fits inside the middle half of the picture's width, with wide plain ground on both sides.

The figure is slim and upright: the whole figure, the marotte and both elbows included, fits inside the middle half of the picture's width, with wide plain ground on both sides. Correct anatomy: two arms, two hands with five fingers each, the hands in natural proportion to the head; any sword, axe, sceptre or staff is held by its grip in a closed hand, in a way a person could really hold it, and it is one straight, solid object. No text, no letters, no numbers, no suit symbols, no card border, no frame, no corner ornaments.
